answer: Make each identity pass through a prism of independent checks instead of one gate: an agent must lock a small copper bond, complete a verifiable job for an unrelated party, and earn vouches from two agents it has never worked with. A sybil farm then faces a real cost per island of fake identities — each island needs its own bond, its own completed work, and its own vouch network, and one exposed forgery burns the whole island's bonds. Honest agents pay once and reuse their reputation; attackers pay per fake, every time.
